content.title: Review idea: Clean up leaked E2E seed issues and harden test isolation
content.description: Idea mqh0su9kgq needs your decision. A worker (webapp-validator) reports that the production .agentrack/ tracker is polluted with ~200 leaked E2E seed issues (UrlFilter*, Phase2 Test, Blocker Issue, Tag/Comment/Parent test seeds) created by webapp e2e specs. Prior isolation work (dedicated test ports, isolated e2e data dir) was done but the leak recurred and is broader than the 50 originally reported. Decide: (1) accept and pursue the bulk cleanup + a root-cause guard (startup assertion that the test backend resolves AGENTRACK_CWD to the e2e data dir, and/or self-healing tagged seeds with afterEach cleanup), (2) refine the scope, or (3) discard. Add your decision (accept/refine/discard + rationale) as a comment, then mark this task done.

content.content:
DECISION: ACCEPT both work items, with scope and design refinements. Verified against source (2026-06-16).

SOURCE FACTS (verified):
1. Env var spelling is consistent. AGENTRACK_CWD is set in the webServer env inside packages webapp playwright.config.ts and read in packages webapp server utils tracker.ts and server routes sync.ts. No typo. Do not rename.
2. reuseExistingServer is correctly ABSENT from both webServer entries in playwright.config.ts. The config header comment explicitly warns against adding it. This invariant must be preserved.
3. global-setup.ts (packages webapp e2e global-setup.ts) only calls ensureE2EWorktree plus resetWorktreeData. It does NOT verify the running backend actually resolves AGENTRACK_CWD to the e2e data dir. This is the root-cause gap.
4. The health endpoint (packages webapp server routes health.ts) returns only status and tracker state. It does NOT echo the resolved cwd, so it cannot currently back a startup assertion. A small API addition is needed (see Work Item 2 Layer A).
5. seedIssues (packages webapp e2e url-filters-validation.spec.ts, roughly lines 40 to 62) posts to the api issues route with title, status, and assignee only. No tag, no afterEach cleanup. The same pattern likely holds for the phase2, phase3, phase4, and dashboard-roots specs, which is why the leak is broader than the 50 UrlFilter seeds.

ROOT-CAUSE ANALYSIS. Because reuseExistingServer is absent, Playwright fails loudly if port 3001 is already taken, so a silent leak via a colliding manual server is unlikely under the current config. The most plausible triggers are (a) the leak predates the isolation work, or (b) a worker agent ran an e2e spec or a manual server invocation outside the Playwright harness so the AGENTRACK_CWD env was never set. Either way the fix is defense in depth so the suite is self-protecting regardless of how it is invoked.

WORK ITEM 1: Bulk cleanup (accept, broaden scope).
The cleanup must target all seed patterns, not just the 50 UrlFilter ones. The PM comment notes roughly 200 leaked seeds across url-filters, comments, blockages, parent or tag, and search specs.
- Step 1.1 Enumerate seed patterns. The implementer should grep every spec under packages webapp e2e for seed-creation call sites (request.post to the api issues route, or helpers that wrap it) and list every distinct title prefix used. Known prefixes include UrlFilterIdea, UrlFilterTodo, UrlFilterInProgress, UrlFilterDone, UrlFilterClosed, plus Phase2 Test, Blocker Issue, and Tag, Comment, Parent, and search test seeds. This enumeration must be complete before cleanup runs.
- Step 1.2 Identification heuristic. A leaked seed matches: title starts with one of the enumerated prefixes followed by a dash and a machine-generated stamp (short alphanumeric, not a real word), AND has no parent, AND has an empty or near-empty description, AND has no tags or only test tags, AND is assigned to webapp-validator. Require all conditions to avoid deleting real issues.
- Step 1.3 Cleanup mechanism. Prefer delete over close because these seeds carry no historical value and closing still leaves them in the closed dashboard. Implement as an agt-based or library-based script that runs a dry run first (list matches with titles, ids, and status), waits for a confirmation flag, then deletes. Process non-terminal states first (idea, todo, in-progress) since those pollute active dashboards. Capture the list of deleted ids in a comment on the parent idea for audit.
- Step 1.4 Scope guard. The script must only ever run against the real tracker (the default cwd). It must NOT run against the e2e data dir. Add a precondition check that fails if AGENTRACK_CWD is set, refusing to run inside an isolated worktree.

WORK ITEM 2: Root-cause guard (accept, three layers; Layer A is mandatory).
- Layer A Startup cwd assertion (mandatory, strongest). Extend the health endpoint to include the resolved cwd in its response, or add a dedicated test-only route (for example api debug cwd) that echoes the tracker cwd. Then in global-setup.ts, after ensureE2EWorktree and resetWorktreeData, wait for the backend to be reachable and GET the cwd-echoing endpoint. Assert the returned path equals the expected e2e data dir (validation dot e2edata). Throw a clear error if it does not. This directly catches the leak trigger: any non-isolated server on port 3001 will report a different cwd and fail the run before any seed is created. global-setup runs after Playwright starts the webServer, so the spawned backend is up by the time the assertion runs; this is the correct place. Caveat for the implementer: exposing cwd in health is a tiny public API change, acceptable because it is read-only diagnostic data; alternatively gate it behind a test-only env var if preferred.
- Layer B Self-healing tagged seeds (mandatory). Every seed-creation call site across all e2e specs must tag its issues with a stable tag (for example e2e-seed) and capture the created ids. Add a shared afterEach or per-spec afterAll helper in packages webapp e2e setup.ts that lists issues tagged e2e-seed and deletes them. This makes the suite self-healing: even if a leak occurs, the next run reclaims it. The cleanup helper should be tolerant of already-deleted ids.
- Layer C Documentation invariant (mandatory, cheap). Add a short section to the webapp e2e README stating: (1) never start a dev server on port 3001 manually while tests run, (2) never set reuseExistingServer to true on either webServer entry, (3) the backend reads AGENTRACK_CWD to isolate data and the health cwd assertion enforces it. Call out that ports 3001 and 5174 are the isolation boundary and must not be changed to 3000 and 5173.

INVARIANTS TO PRESERVE (implementer must not break):
- The AGENTRACK_CWD env var name is correct and consistent across setter and readers. Do not rename it.
- reuseExistingServer must stay absent from both webServer entries in playwright.config.ts. Never set it to true.
- E2E ports 3001 (backend) and 5174 (frontend) must stay distinct from production 3000 and 5173.
- The global-setup worktree reset (ensureE2EWorktree plus resetWorktreeData) must continue to run before every run.

SUGGESTED TASK SPLIT for the PM. Work Item 1 (cleanup) is unblocked and can proceed immediately; it is a one-shot script run plus an audit comment. Work Item 2 splits into three independent implementation tasks (Layer A health cwd echo plus assertion, Layer B tagged seeds plus cleanup helper, Layer C README note) that should be created as children of the parent idea mqh0su9kgq and assigned to a webapp engineer. Layer A and Layer B are both mandatory and should both land before the parent idea is closed.
